REASONING:
Step 1 – Frame the project  
- **Objective / PDO:** “Increase regional collaboration and health system capacities to prevent, detect and respond to health emergencies in Western and Central Africa.” (p. 11‑12)  
- **Scope & Components:** Five countries (Cameroon, CAR, Chad, Republic of Congo, CEMAC) implementing five components (Prevention, Detection, Response, Program Management, Contingent Emergency Response). (p. 11‑13, 15‑16)  
- **Delivery model:** Multiphase Programmatic Approach (MPA) with a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) in each country and a regional PC IU under CEMAC. (p. 17‑18, 44‑45)  
- **Timeline:** Expected approval 29‑Oct‑2025; Expected closing 31‑Dec‑2030; Program closing 31‑Jan‑2032. (p. 6‑7)  
- **Budget / Financing:** Total operation cost US$ 290 million; IDA financing US$ 280 million (150 credit + 130 grant) plus trust‑fund and GFF grants. (p. 7‑9, 36‑38)  
- **Key stakeholders:** World Bank, ministries of health (Cameroon, CAR, Chad, RoC), CEMAC, regional bodies (WAHO, Africa CDC), implementing agencies, donors (GFF, trust funds). (p. 44‑48, 56‑58)  
- **External dependencies:** Regional coordination (RCC), cross‑border data sharing, climate‑change impacts, conflict/FCV, macro‑economic stability, donor funding streams. (p. 2‑4, 22‑24, 31‑33)

Step 2 – Category sweep (candidate risks with supporting text)  

| # | Category | Candidate risk | Evidence (≤25 words) |
|---|----------|----------------|----------------------|
| 1 | technical | Weak laboratory and surveillance capacity may limit detection/response. | “Health systems … are fragile, with limited laboratory diagnostic capabilities and weak surveillance capacity.” |
| 2 | schedule | Delays in recruiting required PIU staff and specialists. | “Legal covenants require recruitment of specialists within 1‑6 months after Effective Date.” |
| 3 | financial | Fiduciary risk – overall financial‑management (FM) residual risk is substantial. | “The overall FM residual risk is assessed as Substantial.” |
| 4 | financial | Procurement risk – substantial due to delays, governance issues, weak contract management. | “Procurement risk is rated Substantial due to delays, governance issues, weak contract management.” |
| 5 | financial | Currency‑exchange risk – DA will be in XAF while financing is in USD. | “Designated Accounts will be opened in XAF for receipt of funds.” |
| 6 | schedule | Conflict/FCV may disrupt field activities and timelines. | “Fragility, Conflict and Violence lead to large displacements and may disrupt service delivery.” |
| 7 | stakeholder | Inadequate stakeholder engagement could exclude vulnerable groups. | “Potential social risks … relate to inadequate stakeholder engagement and exclusion of vulnerable groups.” |
| 8 | stakeholder | Coordination challenges among multiple ministries and regional bodies. | “Implementation arrangements require coordination among multiple ministries; governance challenges identified as key risk.” |
| 9 | political_regulatory | Political instability (e.g., Cameroon’s Northwest/South‑West) may halt services. | “Political instability, particularly in the North‑West and South‑West regions, may disrupt service delivery.” |
|10| environmental | Civil‑works may generate waste, dust, emissions, occupational hazards. | “Environmental risks are substantial and include waste, dust, emission, occupational health and safety.” |
|11| environmental | Climate change may increase floods and disease outbreaks, stressing infrastructure. | “Climate change is a primary driver of health emergencies, increasing floods and disease outbreaks.” |
|12| external | Large IDP flows and security challenges threaten implementation. | “Fragility, Conflict and Violence resulted in 1.1 million new IDPs in the region.” |
|13| political_regulatory | Non‑compliance with ESS/ESCP could trigger sanctions. | “Project prepared under ESF; ESS1,2,3,4,5,10 relevant; compliance essential.” |
|14| external | Macroeconomic constraints and low domestic health funding create financing gaps. | “Macroeconomic outlook challenging; low domestic health funding; high reliance on external aid.” |

Step 3 – Evidence filter  
All 14 risks are directly supported by the cited statements; none are removed.

Step 4 – Assess & mitigate  

| ID | Likelihood (1‑5) | Impact (1‑5) | Mitigation (concise) |
|----|------------------|--------------|----------------------|
| R01 | 4 | 5 | Accelerate lab upgrades, procure equipment, train staff, establish regional lab network, monitor SLIPTA ratings. |
| R02 | 3 | 4 | Set a recruitment tracker, use accelerated hiring, provide incentives, and have standby consultants for critical roles. |
| R03 | 4 | 4 | Update FM manuals, recruit external auditor, conduct quarterly internal audits, provide FM capacity‑building workshops. |
| R04 | 3 | 4 | Hire experienced procurement specialists, conduct early market engagement, use STEP for real‑time tracking, strengthen contract‑management training. |
| R05 | 2 | 3 | Open multi‑currency DA, include exchange‑rate buffer in budget, monitor FX movements, adjust disbursements as needed. |
| R06 | 3 | 4 | Pre‑position supplies, use CERC funds for rapid response, adopt remote training, develop contingency work plans. |
| R07 | 3 | 3 | Implement the Umbrella Stakeholder Engagement Plan, conduct regular community consultations, strengthen GRM and gender‑sensitive outreach. |
| R08 | 3 | 3 | Formalise RCC terms of reference, schedule monthly coordination meetings, share joint work plans, use a single project‑wide information system. |
| R09 | 3 | 4 | Monitor political developments, maintain liaison with local authorities, design flexible activity schedules, earmark contingency funds. |
| R10 | 3 | 3 | Prepare site‑specific ESMPs, enforce waste‑management protocols, train workers on OHS, conduct regular environmental monitoring. |
| R11 | 4 | 4 | Integrate climate‑resilient designs (green building, solar power), embed early‑warning climate data into surveillance, update NAPHS with climate scenarios. |
| R12 | 4 | 4 | Conduct Security Risk Assessments, develop Security Management Plans, hire security specialists, coordinate with UN/NGO security units. |
| R13 | 2 | 3 | Ensure ESCP is fully operational, train staff on ESS requirements, perform periodic compliance audits, embed ESS checks in M&E. |
| R14 | 3 | 4 | Support domestic resource mobilisation (budget coding, medium‑term expenditure frameworks), align health‑security spending with national plans, seek additional donor pledges. |

Step 5 – Consolidate  
All 14 risks are retained; no duplicates identified.
